title: 2005 AMC 12A Problem 9
statement: There are two values of \(a\) for which the equation \(4x^2 + ax + 8x + 9 = 0\) has only one solution for \(x.\) What is the sum of those values of \(a?\)

solutions.text:
The equation is \(4x^2 + (a+8)x + 9 = 0.\) It has one solution when the discriminant vanishes: \[ (a+8)^2 - 4 \cdot 4 \cdot 9 = 0, \] so \((a+8)^2 = 144\) and \(a + 8 = \pm 12.\)

Thus \(a = 4\) or \(a = -20,\) and their sum is \(-16.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: A quadratic has one solution exactly when its discriminant is \(0\)
Write the linear coefficient as \(a + 8\) and set \((a+8)^2 - 4 \cdot 4 \cdot 9 = 0\)
